issue.title: [ACL/PBH] Invalid LAG member configuration when port has active ACL binding

failure.body:
#### Description

SONiC doesn't track port ACL/PBH configuration when adding a LAG member which causes an issues on warm reboot.
We need to add some extra validation to make sure that port can't be made a LAG member when ingress/egress ACL binding is configured. Before moving port to LAG, user should disable active ACL binding, since LAG uses a different dedicated attributes.

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Create ACL table with `Ethernet0` port member
2. Create LAG `PortChannel1` with `Ethernet0` port member
3. Create PBH table with `PortChannel1` LAG member
4. Save config
5. Run warm-reboot

SONiC should fail LAG member configuration when ingress/egress ACL binding is present.

resolution.title: [portsorch]: Prevent LAG member configuration when port has active ACL binding
resolution.description:
Signed-off-by: Nazarii Hnydyn <<EMAIL>>

Add some extra validation to make sure that port can't be made a LAG member when ingress/egress ACL binding is configured.
Before moving port to LAG, user should disable active ACL binding, since LAG uses a different dedicated attributes

fixes Azure/sonic-buildimage#10233

**What I did**
* Prevent LAG member configuration when port has active ACL binding

**Why I did it**
* To fix ACL PORT/LAG config divergency

**How I verified it**
1. Deploy t0 topology
2. Create LAG interface
3. Remove arbitrary port from VLAN
4. Make port LAG member
